paper.title: (Im)possibility of Automated Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
paper.summary: Characterizes semantic automated hallucination detection through identification from positive data, proves universal detection from complete labeled examples, records the Appendix generation consequences, and exposes both a false multiples-family inference and the remaining oracle, query-cost, and probabilistic gaps.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom seventeen-card surface has thirteen fully covered claim groups, one partially covered definition, and three claims with no source-claim coverage. The false no-detector inference is kernel-refuted rather than treated as a proof target; the operational tell-tale oracle, the exact family-query count, and the probabilistic carry-over remain outside full coverage.
specializations: Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, and Theorems A.1--A.2 use an explicit nonempty countable example type; Lemma 3.1 instead receives a concrete surjection from Nat onto the domain.

The formalization is semantic and generally noncomputable, matching the source's explicit removal of computational restrictions; it does not certify effective tell-tale discovery, runtime, convergence rates, or query complexity.
Theorem 2.3 is generalized to an arbitrary example type, but its extra uncountable or empty-domain cases can be vacuous because a complete Nat-indexed labeled enumeration need not exist.
The multiples family uses zero-based predecessor encoding while preserving the source's two displayed containments.
Theorem A.2 is physically owned by GenLimit.Bridges.Paper02ToPaper08 and is available through the global GenLimit umbrella, not the native P08 umbrella alone.
gaps: Definition 4's finite tell-tale predicate is represented, but its operational primitive that returns an enumeration of a tell-tale is not modeled as data, access, or computation.
The 2t-1 fresh family-membership-query claim in footnote 5 has no query-cost declaration.
The prose assertion that the adversarial results carry over to probabilistic presentations has no precise probabilistic theorem or Lean model.
The prose inference after Example 1 is false: singleton tell-tales make the multiples family hallucination-detectable. It is registered as refuted and not planned.

audit_refs.scope: Checksum-pinned arXiv-v2 AI-assisted statement-faithfulness audit covering the full selected P08 source surface, source gaps, semantic qualifications, and the Example 1 refutation. It does not inspect proof bodies or constitute human certification; its immutable evidence labels predate the P00A refactor.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for all eighteen Lean declarations linked from this P08 entry.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Seventeen claim groups: Definitions 1--5; Theorems 2.1, 2.3, A.1, and A.2; Corollary 2.2; Lemma 3.1 together with Algorithm 1; Lemma 3.2 together with Algorithm 2; both displayed Example 1 containments and the following no-detector inference; the 2t-1 family-query bound in footnote 5; and the probabilistic carry-over assertion. Informal Results I--II are folded into the corresponding Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 2.3 cards.
exclusions: Model assumptions, subordinate interface definitions, proof-only intermediate assertions, and unnumbered algorithm steps do not receive standalone cards unless selected explicitly above.

The introduction and conclusion claims that detection is impossible for most collections or that negative labels are fundamentally necessary are rhetorical summaries rather than separately quantified results.

Related-work statements, practical LLM and RLHF analogies, prompts, noisy-feedback extensions, density-relaxation future work, and computational-complexity open questions are outside this minimal pass.
Results imported from Gold, Angluin, Kleinberg--Mullainathan, and Li--Raman--Tewari are not duplicated except for the paper's explicitly numbered Appendix Theorems A.1--A.2.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for this seventeen-card custom scope, not for every sentence or proof step. Printed page locators are the pages of the checksum-pinned 20-page arXiv-v2 author PDF.

claims.title: Hallucination detection in the limit uses finite adaptive candidate-set queries
claims.statement_summary: For every indexed target, exact positive presentation, and candidate set G, a detector may make finitely many adaptive membership queries to G in each round and must eventually decide exactly whether G is contained in the target.

source_refs.locator: Finite adaptive membership-query model preceding Definition 1

source_assessment.notes: The source explicitly imposes no computational restriction beyond finitely many exact adaptive queries per round.

formalization.notes: Detector is defined through the finite OracleTree syntax, so unrestricted set-functional access to G is excluded by type.

lean_links.notes: Unfolding Detector and OracleTree exposes the finite adaptive query restriction; threshold dependence on target, presentation, and candidate set is preserved.

audit_refs.scope: Pinned-source audit of the finite-query and eventual-correctness interfaces; no proof-body or human audit is implied.
Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for the collection-level definition.

claims.title: The paper incorrectly rules out a detector for the multiples family
claims.statement_summary: The prose after Example 1 claims that Theorem 2.1 and Angluin's characterization imply that no hallucination detector exists for the entire family of positive-integer multiples.

source_assessment.notes: The singleton containing the least positive multiple is a finite tell-tale for every language in the family. Hence the family satisfies Angluin's condition and is hallucination-detectable.

formalization.notes: The false source claim is not a proof target. Lean proves its opposite; the refutation link deliberately contributes no formalization coverage.

lean_links.notes: Canonical counterdiagnosis; singleton_index_isTellTale and example_1_angluinCondition are intentionally unlinked proof support.

formalization.notes: Lean states the equivalence on an explicit nonempty countable type; the omitted empty-domain case is outside the source's operational enumeration convention.

claims.title: Algorithm 2 needs 2t-1 fresh family-membership queries in round t
claims.statement_summary: With prior query answers cached, round t checks the new example against the preceding t-1 languages and checks all t examples against the newly introduced language, for 2t-1 fresh family-membership queries.

source_assessment.notes: The count agrees with incremental maintenance of the bounded consistency table: t-1 old-language queries plus t new-language queries.

formalization.notes: Family membership is extensional and uncosted in Lean; no declaration counts fresh queries or certifies this bound.

relations.notes: Quantifies the source Algorithm 2 implementation whose qualitative reduction is formalized separately.

claims.title: Identification in the limit requires consecutive stable and extensionally correct guesses
claims.statement_summary: An identifier succeeds when, after a finite stage, each current index equals the preceding index and its indexed language equals the unknown target for every exact positive presentation.

source_assessment.notes: Adjacent equality on a tail is equivalent to stabilization at one fixed syntactic index, including for families with duplicate language representations.

formalization.notes: The paper-shaped collection-level existential is the canonical endpoint. definition_3_equivalence remains an intentionally unlinked validation helper.

lean_links.notes: Preserves syntactic stability and extensional target correctness as distinct conjuncts.

relations.notes: This appendix definition is extensionally equivalent to the stable-index identification interface used in Theorem 2.1.

claims.statement_summary: Every indexed language has a finite subset T_i such that no family member containing T_i is a proper sublanguage of L_i; the paper additionally declares a primitive that, given i, outputs an enumeration of T_i.

source_assessment.notes: The structural finite-tell-tale property is coherent. The operational oracle is an explicit source access clause, not an error, and its absence from Lean is tracked as a coverage gap.

formalization.notes: Lean exactly represents the structural finite-set predicate, but not a data-bearing or effective primitive that returns an enumeration of the selected tell-tale.

components.summary: Every indexed language has a finite internal certificate excluding every proper sublanguage that contains it.
